_status: DRAFT FOR REVIEW. Not imported into Retell, not deployed. Field names mirror the concepts on Retell's custom-function pages (URL, method, headers, parameters, timeout, retries, speak-during-execution); confirm the exact names on import because the dashboard/API schema was not inspected here. The functions Sol actually imported for the running demo are separate from this draft.
_notes: Replace <YOUR-TUNNEL-HOST> with the public HTTPS host of the tunnel Shobana starts herself. Retell blocks localhost and private addresses.
Set the bearer token (ARIA_RETELL_TOOL_TOKEN) in the Retell dashboard header value, never in this file.
Timeouts are ESTIMATES. A live calendar read takes seconds to tens of seconds; measure before relying on them. lookup_service is local and fast.
max_retry is 0 on purpose: the server is idempotent, but a retry of a slow browser action only adds delay.
Do NOT use 'payload: args only'. The server needs the call object (call_id) to bind options and confirmations to one call.

service_id values come ONLY from the prompt's 'What can be booked online right now' list or from lookup_service. The server validates them against its own allowlist and takes length, price and the Booksy service name from there, never from these arguments.

tools.name: lookup_service
tools.description: Look up a salon service from the caller's own words (for example 'swedish massage 60 minutes' or 'facial'). Returns the website's listed length and price and a short description, whether it can be booked online, or asks you to choose between several matching services or lengths. This is LOCAL information only: it never checks the calendar. Use it when you are unsure which service the caller means; do not call it merely to restate something already in your knowledge section.

query.description: The service as the caller said it, in their words, including a length if they gave one.

tools.name: check_slot
tools.description: Check whether the caller's requested date and start time can be booked for the FULL chosen service, with whom. Call this ONLY when the caller wants an appointment or asks about availability, never for a service, price or product question. Always call it before saying anything about availability. If the time is not available it explains why (closed, service would run past closing, already taken, too soon, named technician booked) and returns up to three genuinely free alternatives, each with an option_id, the service, its length and the technician. Never state availability from your own knowledge.
tools.execution_message_description: Say ONE short sentence, once, as the check starts: 'One moment while I check <technician>'s availability.' if the caller already named a technician, 'One moment while I check availability for <service>.' if only the service is known, otherwise 'One moment while I check availability.' Never guess a name or service the caller has not given. Give no estimate of how long it will take, do not repeat or extend it, add nothing else, and use no filler such as um or uh.

service_id.description: The canonical service_id of the service the caller chose, exactly as listed under 'What can be booked online right now' or returned by lookup_service. Never invent or alter one.

date.description: The requested day as YYYY-MM-DD in the salon's time zone (America/New_York). Resolve words like 'tomorrow' or 'next Tuesday' yourself using the current date, and if it is ambiguous ask the caller first.

time.description: The requested START time in 24-hour HH:MM (for example 14:30). Appointments start on the quarter hour. If the caller said an ambiguous time such as 'at 3', ask whether they mean morning or afternoon before calling.

staff.description: Optional. The technician's name ONLY if the caller asked for a particular person. Omit it otherwise.

tools.name: find_alternatives
tools.description: List up to three genuinely free appointment options for the chosen service starting from a day (and optionally a preferred start time). Use when the caller has no specific time, or asks for other options. Each option has an option_id, the service, its length and the technician. Call only on appointment or availability intent.
tools.execution_message_description: Say ONE short sentence, once, as the search starts: 'One moment while I look for other times with <technician>.' if the caller named a technician, otherwise 'One moment while I look for other times.' Never guess a name the caller has not given. Give no estimate of how long it will take, do not repeat or extend it, add nothing else, and use no filler such as um or uh.

service_id.description: The canonical service_id of the service the caller chose, exactly as listed or returned by lookup_service.

date.description: The first day to search from, YYYY-MM-DD.

time.description: Optional preferred START time in 24-hour HH:MM.

staff.description: Optional. The technician's name ONLY if the caller asked for a particular person.

tools.name: book_slot
tools.description: Book ONE option that this call was offered. The option already fixes the service, length, technician and time; do not try to change them here. Two steps are enforced by the server: the first call returns the exact read-back sentence (status confirmation_required); only after the caller clearly says yes, call again with the same option_id and confirmed=true. Only book when the tool returns status booked_verified or already_booked with ok=true; any other status means the booking is NOT confirmed.
tools.execution_message_description: Tell the caller you are booking it now and checking that it saved, which can take a minute.

option_id.description: The option_id returned by check_slot or find_alternatives in THIS call, exactly as given. Never invent one.

confirmed.description: false (or omitted) to get the read-back sentence; true ONLY after the caller has clearly said yes to that exact read-back.
